prompt: jazz, but deliberately not standard jazz: 11/8 grouped 3+3+3+2, a Balkan band playing jazz changes

requests.ask: lets make jazz.. but i dont want some standard jazz.. i want to do something unique. odd meter, a meter jazz doesn't use - 11/8

changes.why: meter 11/8, the first song in the repo to set meter at all (parseMeter gives 22 steps a bar, pulse 2). Grouped 3+3+3+2 so three long groups are followed by a short one and every bar is cut off a beat early

no groove anywhere on purpose: the swing axis is swingBy(x, 4), which splits the CYCLE into four slices, and in 11/8 that is 2.75 eighths per slice and lands on nothing. Modern odd-metre jazz is played straight and the grouping is the lilt
key E:phrygian with i7 II i7 vii7 (Em7 F Em7 Dm7). Written as bII first, which gave E: in phrygian the second degree is already flat, so II is F major and bII flattens it again to Fb

the instruments are what keep it off Brubeck's turf: gm_clarinet lead, gm_acoustic_bass, piano comping and a darbuka instead of a kit. The darbuka's own sample loudness is already the right balance, doum -16.5 dB, tek -31.1, ka -37.5
the piano stabs land at the END of each group so the comping pushes against the grouping the darbuka states

changes.why: it was not jazz, it was scales. Measured the old lines: 122 notes of solo whose most-repeated three-note shape was 'up a step, down a step', 8 times - no motif at all. Everything melodic is now built on one cell, '0 ~ 3' (a note, a rest, a leap up a fourth), which fills one group of the 3+3+3+2 exactly, transposed, inverted, filled in and fragmented
the old climax was 57% leaps across a two-octave range (degrees 0..12), an arpeggio scramble rather than a line; it now reaches 9 and the lift comes from density and level

sound gm_clarinet>sax and register .5>.25 - the clarinet soundfont measured centroid 1401 Hz and read sharp, and vcsl samples the sax A#1..G#4 (midi 34..68), so at octave 4 the head reached E5 = 76 and was resampled eight semitones above the top sample. At octave 3 the whole line sits at midi 52..67, inside the recording

a written bass solo, not a walk: the first try was '0 1 2 4 5 6 7 6 5 4 2', a scale up and back down, which is the same mistake the sax line had. Eight bars on the full 22-sixteenth grid, the rhythm carried by the rests, 3 to 13 notes a bar
articulation .7>.2 for sustain: the bass layer's hap is one grid step (~0.1 s at this tempo) so the articulation cell is the only thing that lets an upright ring - clip .98 plus a .22 s release

the eight bars are wrapped in <> so one plays per cycle; the bass layer has no phrase material the way melody does, so '[bar] [bar] ...' squeezed all eight into one bar and every bar came out identical

a new four-bar section between solo and strip, because the bass solo arrived with the sax, piano and vibes all vanishing on one downbeat. The sax lays out, the rhythm section carries on, the bass gets busier each bar (4, 6, 9, 10 notes) and is already soloing when the piano stops. The arc taper is now 32.1 > 24.7 > 13.6

requests.ask: bass solo is better but the walk up in progression sounds lazy

changes.why: the hand-off bars climbed by step (0 2 4 5 6 7), which is a scale with rests in it. Rewritten around the song's cell: fourths, thirds and chord tones, ending on the flat second leaning into the solo

solo bars 2, 3, 4 and 6 the same fix - bar 4 now zig-zags up in fourths to reach 9 instead of walking, and bar 6 descends in alternating fourths instead of running down the scale. Over turn and strip the bass is 2 stepwise intervals against 60 leaps

requests.ask: i dont love this song, is it that i just dont like jazz or is it not good? / bridge sounds out of place / this sounds too forced (the alternating-fourths bar) / bass should have more sustain

changes.why: a new section in C major and 4/4: the harmony never moved in 60 bars and the metre never let up. C major is E phrygian's own pitch collection with the tonic moved, so no new note enters; 4/4 at bpm 145 is the same .207 s eighth as 11/8 at bpm 290, so the pulse is identical and only the grouping changes

progression I vi7 ii7 iii7, ending on Em7 - iii7 in C major and the tonic of E phrygian at once, the pivot that hands the song back. It ended on V7, leaving a G7 hanging before a jump to Em7, which is most of why it sat wrong
the 4/4 kit was bd on 1+3 and sd on 2+4, a rock backbeat played on a darbuka, which sounded like a different and cheaper band; now a hand-drum pattern with teks off the beat
no piano and the kit at its bones, so the solo is an arrival: head and solo had carried the same arc letter for 24 bars, nearly half the song. The arc went from A A B C D A to A B B' C D E B'

the alternating-fourths bars were as mechanical as the scales they replaced - 7 4 6 3 5 2 4 is a pattern, not a phrase. Rewritten with mixed motion, each bar its own gesture: 27% stepwise, 44% mid-leap, 29% wide

articulation .7>.15 (and 0 in the solo) for sustain: at .7 the cell gave clip .5 and a .07 s release, about .12 s of sound. Now ~.41 s, which is the bass layer's ceiling - its hap is one grid step and the cell caps clip at 1.1
